paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文字。为每个编号的空白处选择最佳的单词，并在答题卡上标记 A、B、C 或 D。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Weighing yourself regularly is a wonderful way to stay aware of any significant weight fluctuations. 1 , when done too often, this habit can sometimes hurt more than it 2 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 定期称重是了解任何重大体重波动的好方法。然而，如果经常这样做，这种习惯有时会弊大于利。

paragraphs.sourceText: As for me, weighing myself every day caused me to shift my focus from being generally healthy and physically active to focusing 3 on the scale. That was bad to my overall fitness goals. I had gained weight in the form of muscle mass, but thinking only of 4 the number on the scale, I altered my training program. That conflicted with how I needed to train to 5 my goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对我来说，每天称体重使我将注意力从总体健康和身体活跃转移到只关注体重秤。这对我的整体健身目标不利。我的体重以肌肉质量的形式增加了，但一想到要降低体重秤上的数字，我就改变了我的训练计划。这与我实现目标所需的训练方式相冲突。

paragraphs.sourceText: I also found that weighing myself daily did not provide an accurate 6 of the hard work and progress I was making in the gym. It takes about three weeks to a month to notice any significant changes in your weight 7 altering your training program. The most 8 changes will be observed in skill level, strength and inches lost.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我还发现，每天称体重并不能准确描述我在健身房的努力和进步。由于改变训练计划，大约需要三周到一个月的时间才能注意到体重的任何显着变化。最直接的变化将体现在技能水平、力量和损失的英寸数上。

paragraphs.sourceText: For these 9 , I stopped weighing myself every day and switched to a bimonthly weighing schedule 10 . Since weight loss is not my goal, it is less important for me to 11 my weight each week Weighing every other week allows me to observe and 12 any significant weight changes. That tells me whether I need to 13 my training program.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于这些原因，我不再每天称体重，而是改为每两个月称一次体重。由于减肥不是我的目标，因此每周跟踪体重对我来说不太重要。每隔一周称一次体重可以让我观察并解释任何显着的体重变化。这告诉我是否需要调整我的训练计划。

paragraphs.sourceText: I use my bimonthly weigh-in 14 to get information about my nutrition as well. If my training intensity remains the same, but I'm constantly 15 and dropping weight, this is a 16 that I need to increase my daily caloric intake.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我还使用每两个月的体重结果来获取有关我的营养的信息。如果我的训练强度保持不变，但我不断感到饥饿并且体重下降，这表明我需要增加每日热量摄入量。

paragraphs.sourceText: The 17 to stop weighing myself every day has done wonders for my overall health, fitness and well-being. I'm experiencing increased zeal for working out since I no longer carry the burden of a 18 morning weigh-in. I've also experienced greater success in achieving my specific fitness goals, 19 I'm training according to those goals, not the numbers on a scale.
paragraphs.translationZh: 停止每天称体重的决定对我的整体健康、健身和幸福产生了奇迹。由于我不再背负着令人失望的早晨称重的负担，我对锻炼的热情越来越高。我在实现特定的健身目标方面也取得了更大的成功，因为我是根据这些目标而不是体重秤上的数字进行训练。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rather than 20 over the scale, turn your focus to how you look, feel, how your clothes fit and your overall energy level.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不要沉迷于体重，而要把注意力转向你的外表、感觉、衣服是否合身以及你的整体能量水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇课文后的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Unlike so-called basic emotions such as sadness, fear, and anger, guilt emerges a little later, in conjunction with a child's growing grasp of social and moral norms. Children aren't born knowing how to say "I'm sorry"; rather, they learn over time that such statements appease parents and friends — and their own consciences. This is why researchers generally regard so-called moral guilt, in the right amount, to be a good thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与悲伤、恐惧和愤怒等所谓的基本情绪不同，随着孩子对社会和道德规范的掌握不断加深，内疚感会出现得稍晚一些。孩子生来就不会说“对不起”；相反，随着时间的推移，他们了解到这样的言论可以安抚父母和朋友——以及他们自己的良心。这就是为什么研究人员普遍认为适量的所谓道德内疚是一件好事。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the popular imagination, of course, guilt still gets a bad rap. It is deeply uncomfortable — it's the emotional equivalent of wearing a jacket weighted with stones. Yet this understanding is outdated. "There has been a kind of revival or a rethinking about what guilt is and what role guilt can serve, " says Amrisha Vaish, a psychology researcher at the University of Virginia, adding that this revival is part of a larger recognition that emotions aren't binary — feelings that may be advantageous in one context may be harmful in another. Jealousy and anger, for example, may have evolved to alert us to important inequalities. Too much happiness can be destructive.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，在大众的想象中，内疚感仍然受到不好的批评。这是非常不舒服的——这在情感上就相当于穿着一件装满石头的夹克。然而这种理解已经过时了。弗吉尼亚大学心理学研究员阿姆里莎·瓦伊什（Amrisha Vaish）表示，“对于什么是内疚以及内疚能发挥什么作用，人们出现了一种复兴或重新思考。”她补充说，这种复兴是一种更大的认识的一部分，即情绪不是二元的——在一种情况下可能有利的感觉在另一种情况下可能有害。例如，嫉妒和愤怒可能会进化来提醒我们注意重要的不平等。太多的快乐可能具有破坏性。

paragraphs.sourceText: And guilt, by prompting us to think more deeply about our goodness, can encourage humans to make up for errors and fix relationships. Guilt, in other words, can help hold a cooperative species together. It is a kind of social glue.
paragraphs.translationZh: 而内疚感可以促使我们更深入地思考自己的善良，从而鼓励人们弥补错误并修复关系。换句话说，内疚可以帮助让一个合作的物种团结在一起。它是一种社会粘合剂。

paragraphs.sourceText: Viewed in this light, guilt is an opportunity. Work by Tina Malti, a psychology professor at the University of Toronto, suggests that guilt may compensate for an emotional deficiency. In a number of studies, Malti and others have shown that guilt and sympathy may represent different pathways to cooperation and sharing. Some kids who are low in sympathy may make up for that shortfall by experiencing more guilt, which can rein in their nastier impulses. And vice versa: High sympathy can substitute for low guilt.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从这个角度来看，内疚是一个机会。多伦多大学心理学教授蒂娜·马尔蒂的研究表明，内疚可以弥补情感上的缺陷。在许多研究中，马尔蒂和其他人表明，内疚和同情可能代表着合作和分享的不同途径。一些同情心较低的孩子可能会通过经历更多的内疚感来弥补这种不足，这可以抑制他们更恶劣的冲动。反之亦然：高度同情可以替代低度内疚。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a 2014 study, for example, Malti looked at 244 children. Using caregiver assessments and the children's self-observations, she rated each child's overall sympathy level and his or her tendency to feel negative emotions after moral transgressions. Then the kids were handed chocolate coins, and given a chance to share them with an anonymous child. For the low-sympathy kids, how much they shared appeared to turn on how inclined they were to feel guilty. The guilt-prone ones shared more, even though they hadn't magically become more sympathetic to the other child's deprivation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，在 2014 年的一项研究中，Malti 研究了 244 名儿童。通过看护者的评估和孩子们的自我观察，她对每个孩子的整体同情心水平以及他或她在道德违规后感受到负面情绪的倾向进行了评估。然后孩子们收到了巧克力硬币，并有机会与一位匿名的孩子分享。对于缺乏同情心的孩子来说，他们分享的程度似乎取决于他们感到内疚的倾向。那些容易感到内疚的孩子分享了更多，尽管他们并没有神奇地变得更加同情另一个孩子的剥夺。

paragraphs.sourceText: "That's good news," Malti says. "We can be prosocial because we caused harm and we feel regret."
paragraphs.translationZh: “这是个好消息，”马尔蒂说。 “我们可以变得亲社会，因为我们造成了伤害并且我们感到遗憾。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Forests give us shade, quiet and one of the harder challenges in the fight against climate change. Even as we humans count on forests to soak up a good share of the carbon dioxide we produce, we are threatening their ability to do so. The climate change we are hastening could one day leave us with forests that emit more carbon than they absorb.
paragraphs.translationZh: 森林为我们提供荫凉、安静，也是应对气候变化的艰巨挑战之一。尽管我们人类依靠森林吸收我们产生的大部分二氧化碳，但我们正在威胁他们这样做的能力。我们正在加速的气候变化有一天可能会让我们的森林排放的碳多于吸收的碳。

paragraphs.sourceText: Thankfully, there is a way out of this trap — but it involves striking a subtle balance. Helping forests flourish as valuable "carbon sinks" long into the future may require reducing their capacity to absorb carbon now. California is leading the way, as it does on so many climate efforts, in figuring out the details.
paragraphs.translationZh: 值得庆幸的是，有一种方法可以摆脱这个陷阱，但它需要取得微妙的平衡。帮助森林在未来很长一段时间内作为有价值的“碳汇”蓬勃发展可能需要降低其现在吸收碳的能力。正如它在许多气候努力中所做的那样，加州在弄清楚细节方面处于领先地位。

paragraphs.sourceText: The state's proposed Forest Carbon Plan aims to double efforts to thin out young trees and clear brush in parts of the forest. This temporarily lowers carbon-carrying capacity. But the remaining trees draw a greater share of the available moisture, so they grow and thrive, restoring the forest's capacity to pull carbon from the air. Healthy trees are also better able to fend off insects. The landscape is rendered less easily burnable. Even in the event of a fire, fewer trees are consumed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该州提出的森林碳计划旨在加倍努力稀疏幼树并清除部分森林的灌木丛。这会暂时降低碳承载能力。但剩下的树木吸收了更多的可用水分，因此它们生长茂盛，恢复了森林从空气中吸收碳的能力。健康的树木也能更好地抵御昆虫。景观变得不易燃烧。即使发生火灾，烧毁的树木也更少。

paragraphs.sourceText: The need for such planning is increasingly urgent. Already, since 2010, drought and insects have killed over 100 million trees in California, most of them in 2016 alone, and wildfires have burned hundreds of thousands of acres.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对此类规划的需求日益迫切。自 2010 年以来，干旱和昆虫已经导致加利福尼亚州超过 1 亿棵树死亡，其中大多数仅在 2016 年就被杀死，野火也烧毁了数十万英亩土地。

paragraphs.sourceText: California plans to treat 35,000 acres of forest a year by 2020, and 60,000 by 2030 — financed from the proceeds of the state's emissions-permit auctions. That's only a small share of the total acreage that could benefit, about half a million acres in all, so it will be vital to prioritize areas at greatest risk of fire or drought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加州计划到 2020 年每年治理 35,000 英亩森林，到 2030 年治理 60,000 英亩森林，资金来自该州排放许可证拍卖的收益。这仅占受益总面积的一小部分（总共约50万英亩），因此优先考虑火灾或干旱风险最大的地区至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: The strategy also aims to ensure that carbon in woody material removed from the forests is locked away in the form of solid lumber or burned as biofuel in vehicles that would otherwise run on fossil fuels. New research on transportation biofuels is already under way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该战略还旨在确保从森林中采伐的木质材料中的碳以实心木材的形式储存起来，或作为生物燃料在原本使用化石燃料的车辆中燃烧。关于交通生物燃料的新研究已经在进行中。

paragraphs.sourceText: State governments are well accustomed to managing forests, but traditionally they've focused on wildlife, watersheds and opportunities for recreation. Only recently have they come to see the vital part forests will have to play in storing carbon. California's plan, which is expected to be finalized by the governor next year, should serve as a model.
paragraphs.translationZh: 州政府非常习惯于管理森林，但传统上他们更关注野生动物、流域和休闲机会。直到最近，他们才开始认识到森林在碳储存方面所发挥的重要作用。加州的计划预计将于明年由州长最终确定，应该作为典范。

paragraphs.sourceText: American farmers have been complaining of labor shortages for several years. The complaints are unlikely to stop without an overhaul of immigration rules for farm workers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 多年来，美国农民一直抱怨劳动力短缺。如果不彻底改革农场工人的移民规则，这些抱怨就不可能停止。

paragraphs.sourceText: Congress has obstructed efforts to create a more straightforward visa for agricultural workers that would let foreign workers stay longer in the U.S. and change jobs within the industry. If this doesn't change, American businesses, communities, and consumers will be the losers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 国会阻碍了为农业工人创建更简单的签证的努力，该签证将使外国工人在美国停留更长时间并在该行业内更换工作。如果这一点不改变，美国企业、社区和消费者将成为输家。

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps half of U.S. farm laborers are undocumented immigrants. As fewer such workers enter the country, the characteristics of the agricultural workforce are changing. Today's farm laborers, while still predominantly born in Mexico, are more likely to be settled rather than migrating and more likely to be married than single. They're also aging. At the start of this century, about one-third of crop workers were over the age of 35. Now, more than half are. And picking crops is hard on older bodies. One oft-debated cure for this labor shortage remains as implausible as it's been all along: Native U.S. workers won't be returning to the farm.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许一半的美国农场工人是无证移民。随着进入该国的此类工人越来越少，农业劳动力的特征正在发生变化。今天的农场劳动者虽然仍然主要出生在墨西哥，但更有可能定居​​而不是移民，更有可能结婚而不是单身。他们也在变老。本世纪初，大约三分之一的农作物工人年龄在 35 岁以上。现在，这一数字超过一半。对于老年人来说，采摘庄稼是很困难的。解决劳动力短缺问题的一个经常被争论的解决方案仍然像一直以来一样令人难以置信：美国本土工人不会返回农场。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mechanization isn't the answer, either — not yet, at least. Production of corn, cotton, rice, soybeans, and wheat has been largely mechanized, but many high-value, labor-intensive crops, such as strawberries, need labor. Even dairy farms, where robots do a small share of milking, have a long way to go before they're automated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 机械化也不是答案——至少目前还不是。玉米、棉花、水稻、大豆和小麦的生产已基本机械化，但草莓等许多高价值、劳动密集型作物需要劳动力。即使是由机器人承担一小部分挤奶工作的奶牛场，在实现自动化之前还有很长的路要走。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a result, farms have grown increasingly reliant on temporary guest workers using the H-2A visa to fill the gaps in the agricultural workforce. Starting around 2012, requests for the visas rose sharply; from 2011 to 2016 the number of visas issued more than doubled.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，农场越来越依赖使用 H-2A 签证的临时客工来填补农业劳动力的缺口。从2012年左右开始，签证申请量急剧增加；从2011年到2016年，签发的签证数量增加了一倍多。

paragraphs.sourceText: The H-2A visa has no numerical cap, unlike the H-2B visa for nonagricultural work, which is limited to 66,000 a year. Even so, employers complain they aren't given all the workers they need. The process is cumbersome, expensive and unreliable. One survey found that bureaucratic delays led the average H-2A worker to arrive on the job 22 days late. The shortage is compounded by federal immigration raids, which remove some workers and drive others underground.
paragraphs.translationZh: H-2A签证没有数量上限，与非农业工作的H-2B签证每年的数量上限为66,000个不同。即便如此，雇主还是抱怨他们没有获得所需的全部工人。该过程繁琐、昂贵且不可靠。一项调查发现，官僚主义拖延导致 H-2A 员工平均晚到工作 22 天。联邦移民突击搜查导致人员短缺，一些工人被赶走，另一些则被迫转入地下。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a 2012 survey, 71 percent of tree-fruit growers and nearly 80 percent of raisin and berry growers said they were short of labor. Some western farmers have responded by moving operations to Mexico. From 1998 to 2000, 14.5 percent of the fruit Americans consumed was imported. Little more than a decade later, the share of imports was 25.8 percent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在 2012 年的一项调查中，71% 的树果种植者和近 80% 的葡萄干和浆果种植者表示，他们缺乏劳动力。一些西方农民的应对措施是将业务转移到墨西哥。从 1998 年到 2000 年，美国人消费的水果中有 14.5% 是进口的。十多年后，进口份额达到 25.8%。

paragraphs.sourceText: In effect, the U.S. can import food or it can import the workers who pick it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 实际上，美国可以进口食品，也可以进口采摘食品的工人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Dia Mirza and Adrian Grenier have a message for you: It's easy to beat plastic. They're part of a bunch of celebrities starring in a new video for World Environment Day — encouraging you, the consumer, to swap out your single-use plastic staples to combat the plastics crisis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 阿诺·施瓦辛格、迪亚·米尔扎和阿德里安·格尼尔向您传达一条信息：打败塑料很容易。他们是众多名人在世界环境日拍摄的新视频中的一员，鼓励消费者更换一次性塑料钉书钉，以应对塑料危机。

paragraphs.sourceText: The key messages that have been put together for World Environment Day do include a call for governments to enact legislation to curb single-use plastics. But the overarching message is directed at individuals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界环境日的关键信息确实包括呼吁各国政府颁布立法来限制一次性塑料制品。但最重要的信息是针对个人的。

paragraphs.sourceText: My concern with leaving it up to the individual, however, is our limited sense of what needs to be achieved. On their own, taking our own bags to the grocery store or quitting plastic straws, for example, will accomplish little and require very little of us. They could even be harmful, satisfying a need to have "done our bit" without ever progressing onto bigger, bolder, more effective actions — a kind of "moral licensing" that eases our concerns and stops us doing more and asking more of those in charge.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，我担心将其留给个人，因为我们对需要实现的目标的认识有限。例如，仅凭自己的袋子去杂货店或戒掉塑料吸管，收效甚微，对我们的要求也很少。它们甚至可能是有害的，满足了“尽自己的一份力量”的需要，却没有采取更大规模、更大胆、更有效的行动——一种“道德许可”，可以减轻我们的担忧，阻止我们做更多的事情，并向负责人提出更多的要求。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the conversation around our environment and our responsibility toward it remains centered on shopping bags and straws, we're ignoring the balance of power that implies that as "consumers" we must shop sustainably, rather than as "citizens" hold our governments and industries to account to push for real systemic change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然围绕我们的环境和我们对环境的责任的讨论仍然集中在购物袋和吸管上，但我们忽视了权力平衡，这意味着作为“消费者”我们必须可持续地购物，而不是作为“公民”要求我们的政府和行业负责推动真正的系统性变革。

paragraphs.sourceText: It's important to acknowledge that the environment isn't everyone's priority — or even most people's. We shouldn't expect it to be. In her latest book, Why Good People Do Bad Environmental Things, Elizabeth R. DeSombre argues that the best way to collectively change the behavior of large numbers of people is for the change to be structural.
paragraphs.translationZh: 重要的是要承认，环境并不是每个人（甚至大多数人）的首要任务。我们不应该期望它会这样。伊丽莎白·R·德松布尔 (Elizabeth R. DeSombre) 在她的最新著作《为什么好人会做坏事》中指出，集体改变大量人行为的最佳方式是进行结构性改变。

paragraphs.sourceText: This might mean implementing policy such as a plastic tax that adds a cost to environmentally problematic action, or banning single-use plastics altogether. India has just announced it will "eliminate all single-use plastic in the country by 2022." There are also incentive-based ways of making better environmental choices easier, such as ensuring recycling is at least as easy as trash disposal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这可能意味着实施塑料税等政策，增加环境问题行动的成本，或者完全禁止一次性塑料。印度刚刚宣布将“到 2022 年消除该国所有一次性塑料制品”。还有一些基于激励的方法可以让更好的环境选择变得更容易，例如确保回收至少像垃圾处理一样容易。

paragraphs.sourceText: DeSombre isn't saying people should stop caring about the environment. It's just that individual actions are too slow, she says, for that to be the only, or even primary, approach to changing widespread behavior.
paragraphs.translationZh: 德松布尔并不是说人们应该停止关心环境。她说，只是个人行动太慢，这不是改变普遍行为的唯一甚至主要方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: None of this is about writing off the individual. It's just about putting things into perspective. We don't have time to wait. We need progressive policies that shape collective action, alongside engaged citizens pushing for change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 所有这些都不是要注销个人。这只是要正确看待事物。我们没有时间等待。我们需要制定集体行动的进步政策，同时需要积极参与的公民推动变革。

paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文本，并将左栏中的每个编号项目与右栏中的相应信息相匹配。右栏中有两个额外的选项。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: How seriously should parents take kids' opinions when searching for a home?
paragraphs.translationZh: 在找房时，父母应该如何认真考虑孩子的意见？

paragraphs.sourceText: In choosing a new home, Camille McClain's kids had a single demand: a backyard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在选择新家时，卡米尔·麦克莱恩的孩子们只有一个需求：后院。

paragraphs.sourceText: McClain's little ones aren't the only kids who have an opinion when it comes to housing, and in many cases youngsters' views weigh heavily on parents' real estate decisions, according to a 2018 Harris Poll survey of more than 2,000 U.S. adults.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2018 年哈里斯民意调查对 2000 多名美国成年人进行的一项调查显示，麦克莱恩的孩子并不是唯一在住房问题上有意见的孩子，而且在许多情况下，孩子们的观点对父母的房地产决定影响很大。

paragraphs.sourceText: While more families buck an older-generation proclivity to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions, realty agents and psychologists have mixed views about the financial, personal and long-term effects kids' opinions may have.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然越来越多的家庭反对老一辈倾向于让孩子对房地产决策一无所知，但房地产经纪人和心理学家对孩子的意见可能产生的财务、个人和长期影响的看法不一。

paragraphs.sourceText: The idea of involving children in a big decision is a great idea because it can help them feel a sense of control and ownership in what can be an overwhelming process, said Ryan Hooper, clinical psychologist in Chicago.
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥临床心理学家瑞安·胡珀 (Ryan Hooper) 表示，让孩子参与重大决策是一个好主意，因为它可以帮助他们在这个可能是压倒性的过程中感受到控制感和主人翁感。

paragraphs.sourceText: "Children may face serious difficulties in coping with significant moves, especially if it removes them from their current school or support system," he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说：“孩子们在应对重大举措时可能会面临严重困难，特别是如果这将他们从目前的学校或支持系统中剔除的话。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Greg Jaroszewski, a real estate broker with Gagliardo Realty Associates, said he's not convinced that kids should be involved in selecting a home — but their opinions should be considered in regards to proximity to friends and social activities, if possible.
paragraphs.translationZh: Gagliardo Realty Associates 的房地产经纪人格雷格·雅罗斯泽夫斯基 (Greg Jaroszewski) 表示，他不认为孩子应该参与选择房屋，但如果可能的话，应该在与朋友的距离和社交活动方面考虑他们的意见。

paragraphs.sourceText: Younger children should feel like they're choosing their home — without actually getting a choice in the matter, said Adam Bailey, real estate attorney based in New York.
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽约房地产律师亚当·贝利 (Adam Bailey) 表示，年幼的孩子应该感觉自己正在选择自己的家，但实际上并没有选择权。

paragraphs.sourceText: Asking them questions about what they like about the backyard of a potential home will make them feel like they're being included in the decision-making process, Bailey said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 贝利说，向他们询问他们喜欢潜在房屋后院的哪些方面会让他们感觉自己被纳入了决策过程。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many of the aspects of homebuying aren't a consideration for children, said Tracey Hampson, a real estate agent based in Santa Clarita, Calif. And placing too much emphasis on their opinions can ruin a fantastic home purchase.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加利福尼亚州圣克拉丽塔的房地产经纪人特雷西·汉普森 (Tracey Hampson) 表示，购房的许多方面都不是儿童考虑的因素。过分强调他们的意见可能会毁掉一次美妙的购房。

paragraphs.sourceText: "Speaking with your children before you make a real estate decision is wise, but I wouldn't base the purchasing decision solely on their opinions," Hampson said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 汉普森说：“在做出房地产决定之前与您的孩子交谈是明智的，但我不会仅根据他们的意见做出购买决定。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The other issue is that many children — especially older ones — may base their real estate knowledge on HGTV shows, said Aaron Norris of The Norris Group in Riverside, Calif.
paragraphs.translationZh: 加利福尼亚州河滨市诺里斯集团 (The Norris Group) 的亚伦·诺里斯 (Aaron Norris) 表示，另一个问题是，许多孩子，尤其是年龄较大的孩子，可能会通过 HGTV 节目获得房地产知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: "They love Chip and Joanna Gaines just as much as the rest of us," he said. "HGTV has seriously changed how people view real estate. It's not shelter, it's a lifestyle. With that mindset change come some serious money consequences."
paragraphs.translationZh: “他们和我们其他人一样热爱奇普和乔安娜·盖恩斯，”他说。 “HGTV 严重改变了人们对房地产的看法。它不是住所，而是一种生活方式。随着心态的改变，会带来一些严重的金钱后果。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Kids tend to get stuck in the features and the immediate benefits to them personally, Norris said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 诺里斯说，孩子们往往会被这些功能以及对他们个人带来的直接好处所困。

paragraphs.sourceText: Parents need to remind their children that their needs and desires may change over time, said Julie Gurner, a real estate analyst with FitSmallBusiness.com.
paragraphs.translationZh: FitSmallBusiness.com 的房地产分析师朱莉·古纳 (Julie Gurner) 表示，父母需要提醒孩子，他们的需求和愿望可能会随着时间而改变。

paragraphs.sourceText: "Their opinions can change tomorrow," Gurner said. "Harsh as it may be to say, that decision should likely not be made contingent on a child's opinions, but rather made for them with great consideration into what home can meet their needs best — and give them an opportunity to customize it a bit and make it their own."
paragraphs.translationZh: “他们的意见明天可能会改变，”古纳说。 “尽管这么说可能很严厉，但这个决定可能不应该根据孩子的意见而做出，而是应该为他们做出充分考虑，什么样的家最能满足他们的需求——并给他们一个机会对其进行一些定制，使其成为他们自己的家。”

paragraphs.sourceText: This advice is more relevant now than ever before, even as more parents want to embrace the ideas of their children, despite the current housing crunch.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管目前住房紧缩，但越来越多的父母希望接受孩子的想法，这一建议现在比以往任何时候都更加重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 将下列文字翻译成中文。将您的翻译写在答题卡上。 （15分）

paragraphs.sourceText: It is easy to underestimate English writer James Herriot. He had such a pleasant, readable style that one might think that anyone could imitate it. How many times have I heard people say, "I could write a book. I just haven't the time." Easily said. Not so easily done. James Herriot, contrary to popular opinion, did not find it easy in his early days of, as he put it, "having a go at the writing game". While he obviously had an abundance of natural talent, the final, polished work that he gave to the world was the result of years of practising, re-writing and reading. Like the majority of authors, he had to suffer many disappointments and rejections along the way, but these made him all the more determined to succeed. Everything he achieved in life was earned the hard way and his success in the literary field was no exception.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人们很容易低估英国作家詹姆斯·赫里奥特。他的风格如此令人愉悦、可读性强，以至于人们可能会认为任何人都可以模仿。我有多少次听到人们说：“我可以写一本书。我只是没有时间。”轻松地说。没那么容易做到。与流行的观点相反，詹姆斯·赫里奥特（James Herriot）发现在他的早期“尝试写作游戏”并不容易。虽然他显然拥有丰富的天赋，但他向世界呈现的最终精美作品是多年练习、重写和阅读的结果。和大多数作家一样，他一路上也经历过许多失望和拒绝，但这让他更加坚定了成功的决心。他一生所取得的一切成就都是来之不易的，他在文学领域的成功也不例外。

options.translationZh: 指出购房时应考虑孩子的朋友和社交活动等方面。

options.sourceText: believes that homebuying decisions should be based on children's needs rather than their opinions.
options.translationZh: 认为购房决定应该基于孩子的需求而不是他们的意见。

options.sourceText: assumes that many children's views on real estate are influenced by the media.
options.translationZh: 假设许多孩子对房地产的看法受到媒体的影响。

options.sourceText: remarks that significant moves may pose challenges to children.
options.translationZh: 表示重大举措可能会给儿童带来挑战。

options.sourceText: says that it is wise to leave kids in the dark about real estate decisions.
options.translationZh: 说让孩子们对房地产决策一无所知是明智的。

options.sourceText: advises that home purchases should not be based only on children's opinions.
options.translationZh: 建议购房不应仅基于孩子的意见。

options.sourceText: thinks that children should be given a sense of involvement in homebuying decisions.
